description: Find insider transactions reported to the SEC on Form 4, from 2020 to today (country=US, the default), or in the registers of the Netherlands (AFM), Germany (BaFin), Belgium (FSMA), Sweden (FI) and Spain (CNMV) with country=NL, DE, BE, SE or ES, the five European registers together with country=EU, or all of them with country=all. European rows are one line of the regulator's register each, in the currency of the filing with a euro value next to it, and every row names its source (source, source_url); cite it when you use a row. For Form 4: Filter by ticker, company, insider name, role, buy or sell, a date range, a minimum value and Rule 10b5-1 plans; sort newest first or by largest value. By default the lines of one filing with the same transaction code are combined into one row (total shares, weighted average price, total value, number of lines). For 'the largest recent insider purchases' use type=buy and sort=largest_value. Each row has the insider and their role, the dates, shares, price, value in USD, whether it was a planned trade, source_url (the filing at the SEC) and company_url (our company page, when there is one). Open-market purchases and sales since mid-June 2026 also carry the latest price and the change from the price in the filing to that latest price: a measurement of the share price, not advice.

country.description: Which register: US = SEC Form 4 since 2020 (default); NL = the Dutch AFM registers; DE = BaFin (Germany); BE = FSMA (Belgium); SE = Finansinspektionen (Sweden); ES = CNMV (Spain); EU = the five European registers together (for a question about Europe, sorted on the euro value with sort=largest_value); all = every register together, as the InsiderRadar register page shows it (US filings there start on 15 June 2026). For anything but US, ticker, role, planned, group_by_filing and min_value_usd do not apply: use issuer for the company and min_value_eur for a minimum amount.

days.description: Look back this many days from today. Default 90. Leave out when you give from.

group_by_filing.description: true (default) = one row per filing and transaction code; false = every line of the filing as its own row.

insider.description: Part of the reporting person's name as filed, e.g. Huang. SEC filings usually write the last name first (HUANG JEN HSUN).

issuer.description: Part of the issuer's company name, e.g. Nvidia. Use ticker when you know it.

limit.description: How many rows to return. Default 20.

min_value_eur.description: Only rows worth at least this many euros, converted at the ECB reference rate of the trade date. For any country except US.

min_value_usd.description: Only rows worth at least this many US dollars (shares × price as filed).

planned.description: Rule 10b5-1 trading plans: a trade marked planned_trade=true was made under a plan the insider set up in advance, so its timing was fixed earlier. exclude = leave planned trades out, only = only planned trades, all = both. The checkbox exists on Form 4 since April 2023; older filings have planned_trade=null and count as not planned. Default all.

role.description: Only filings by a director, an officer, or an owner of more than 10% of the company.

sort.description: newest = newest filing first (default); largest_value = highest value in USD first.

ticker.description: The issuer's exchange ticker, e.g. NVDA (case does not matter). Matched on the company's SEC identifier (CIK), so filings made under an earlier ticker are included (META also finds the FB years).

type.description: buy = open-market purchases (code P), sell = open-market sales (code S), all = every transaction (also awards, option exercises, tax withholding, gifts). Default all.

name: search_insider_transactions
title: Search insider transactions (SEC Form 4 and the European registers)
